title: Python: run lifecycle and model spend
summary: The run lifecycle stands on sound durable mechanics. A pure, unit-tested transition table (domain/runs.py) is enforced by apply_command under job-then-run row locks. Claims and heartbeats use database time and a rising generation, and idempotency receipts are serialized by advisory locks. Completion is decided from recorded evidence, and an integer micro-dollar ledger reserves before dispatch and keeps uncertain attempts open. Comments explain why and cite their decisions. The cost sits in two hubs. goal_loop.py (782 lines) combines tool assembly, prompts, dispatch, lease keeping and settlement, and workflow_runner plus ten test files reach its private names, with function-local imports to dodge a cycle. Its _finish decides the fate of every pass by membership in string sets: it fails any code PAUSE_FOR lacks, and it reads the run status three times. In runs.py, admit_run (15 parameters, with a binding typed Any that four shapes satisfy) and apply_command (11 parameters, positional job tuple) carry admission and transition plumbing. Job-row writes, version reads and system commands issued as Actor.USER are spread over six modules beside the command table. Types stop at the database edge: 73 connection: Any parameters, positional rows, and an untyped policy snapshot read seven ways. State vocabularies are restated as literals, and run_projection.py (664 lines) also hosts a display redaction weaker than the log redaction. I read the metric leads on validate_proposal, verify_candidate and ModelAdmission.admit and judged them acceptable, since they are flat guard sequences or one atomic reservation. Priorities, in order: a typed stop-code table with a pure _finish decision; one shared redaction; parameter objects for admission and worker commands that keep lock order, fencing and receipt fingerprints; and a split of goal_loop along its seams.

scores.why: Project ruff and mypy strict pass, but no complexity or positional-argument gate exists, and Any at the database edge stops strict typing from catching errors.
Other modules use goal_loop.py's private names through cyclic local imports, run_projection.py hosts redaction that 7 modules use, and the API imports the worker loop.
Two files exceed 650 lines. admit_run has 124 lines and 15 parameters; plan_tools has 121 lines, apply_command 97, run_goal 90, read_inspector 89 and _finish 86.
Many small pure helpers (worst_case_cost, classify_status, validate_proposal, WakeClock), but admit_run, apply_command, run_goal and _finish mix decisions with I/O.
The layout follows DH-03, but run and job state are written from four modules beside the command table rather than through it.

Database-time leases, database-enforced fencing, receipts and a reserve-first ledger set the example; the gaps are unbounded re-claims, an unawaited keeper task and views without a consistent snapshot.
Comments consistently explain why and cite decisions and stories; run_goal and _finish lack contract docstrings, and one module docstring is wrong.
73 connection: Any parameters, positional rows, an untyped policy snapshot and a binding typed Any that SimpleNamespace satisfies; enums exist but stop at the edges.
Stop codes are strings that fail by default, ledger conflicts raise plain ValueError, and a crashing pass is re-claimed forever; cancellation itself propagates correctly.
The pure parts have unit tests named for behaviors and tests/db covers behavior broadly, but settlement and transition rules have no unit seam and tests depend on private names.
Correct where it matters most, but slow to change: hub functions, string vocabularies and untyped rows make each lifecycle edit a multi-file change that only the db profile can prove.

strengths.title: One canonical transition table, enforced where the change is written
strengths.evidence: services/agent/src/autobots/domain/runs.py:24-125 defines NORMAL_EXITS, COMMANDS, COMMAND_SOURCES and next_status. apply_command (services/agent/src/autobots/application/runs.py:404-447) evaluates them under the job and run row locks, with the expected version. record_transition (services/agent/src/autobots/application/runs.py:315-325) writes status, version and event together. Unit tests cover them in services/agent/tests/test_contracts.py:103-159.

strengths.title: Ownership by database time and a rising generation
strengths.evidence: services/agent/src/autobots/application/worker_leases.py:76-104 claims with 'for update of j skip locked', increments the generation and sets the expiry from clock_timestamp(). heartbeat (worker_leases.py:142-154) extends only a live lease, and revive_lease (worker_leases.py:123-139) fails once anyone else has claimed the job. services/agent/src/autobots/application/runs.py:381-387 checks ownership under the job row lock in the writing transaction. services/agent/src/autobots/adapters/checkpoints.py:59-75 makes the database refuse stale checkpoint writes.

strengths.title: A conservative integer ledger that reserves before dispatch
strengths.evidence: services/agent/src/autobots/application/model_admission.py:60-70 rounds the worst-case cost up, in micro-dollars. admit (model_admission.py:105-186) serializes each workspace on an advisory lock and checks slots, run and day budgets before inserting the reservation. Only fail_before_acceptance releases money (model_admission.py:242-248); mark_uncertain keeps it (model_admission.py:250-259).

strengths.title: Idempotent commands with serialized receipts
strengths.evidence: services/agent/src/autobots/application/runs.py:74-133: request_hash normalizes content, and existing_receipt takes a transaction advisory lock on the exact key, so concurrent duplicates wait and replay, while different content raises IdempotencyConflict. Comments explain fingerprint compatibility with older receipts (services/agent/src/autobots/application/runs.py:210-216).

strengths.title: Retry policy and sleep detection as small units with injected time
strengths.evidence: services/agent/src/autobots/application/model_attempts.py:55-71 classifies HTTP statuses in one table. call_with_policy (model_attempts.py:108-155) bounds retries by count, wait cap and root deadline, never retries an uncertain outcome and never invents a charge. services/agent/tests/test_model_attempts.py:105-216 states each rule as a test named for its behavior. WakeClock (services/agent/src/autobots/application/worker_leases.py:19-47) takes injected clocks and is tested in test_wake_clock.py.

strengths.title: Completion decided from records, not from model claims
strengths.evidence: plan_view (services/agent/src/autobots/application/plans.py:138-151) decides completion from recorded evidence. verify_candidate (services/agent/src/autobots/application/verification.py:35-77) reads artifacts back from storage and writes no verdict. services/agent/src/autobots/application/goal_loop.py:462-481 commits the verdict with the transition, so a worker that lost the run records nothing.

strengths.title: Public projection through the contract
strengths.evidence: project_event (services/agent/src/autobots/application/run_projection.py:93-108) validates each stored payload against the RunEvent contract and drops what doesn't fit while the cursor advances. read_inspector (services/agent/src/autobots/application/run_projection.py:576-664) reads typed columns only, never tool arguments or partial model output.

strengths.title: Comments that explain why and cite their source
strengths.evidence: services/agent/src/autobots/application/goal_loop.py:269-270 (Decision 0023 on citing criteria by ID), services/agent/src/autobots/application/run_usage.py:77-87 (the clock behavior observed in US-12.5), services/agent/src/autobots/application/compaction.py:1-6 (what compaction may never lose), services/agent/src/autobots/application/recovery.py:18-20, services/agent/src/autobots/application/worker_inference.py:1-5.

findings.title: goal_loop.py is a seven-concern hub that other modules use through private names

locations.note: loop_registry: tool assembly, also used by tool_catalog.py and workflow_runner.py
_scope_guidance and _opening: prompt text plus an experts query
_drive: job dispatch; imports workflow_runner inside the function (line 434) to avoid a cycle
_keep_lease: lease keeping, imported by workflow_runner.py and tests/db/wake_check.py
_finish: settlement, called 8 times here and 6 times from workflow_runner.py
imports _finish, _keep_lease, _result and _run_status; imports _drive inside a function at line 299
the tool catalog imports the worker loop for loop_registry
the API imports the worker loop module for the 7-line execution_block query

findings.evidence: 782 lines and 22 top-level definitions (19 functions, 3 classes): tool registry (162-197), graph construction (208-247), prompts and an experts query (250-288), the pass (291-380), job dispatch (383-441), candidate settlement (444-488), lease keeping (491-547) and run settlement (550-782). Consumers depend on the private half. workflow_runner.py imports four underscore names at module level and _drive inside drive_child, while goal_loop imports run_workflow inside _drive, a cycle that only function-local imports avoid. Besides workflow_runner.py, ten test files import goal_loop's private names: nine tests/db scripts (_finish, _drive, _settle_children, _settle_candidate, _keep_lease, _scope_guidance) and services/agent/tests/test_plans.py (_opening), counted by parsing every import statement.
findings.impact: Settlement and the keeper are an undeclared API: reshaping _finish or _keep_lease breaks the workflow runner and ten test files, and import order becomes part of correctness. The API process and the tool catalog load deepagents and langgraph through this module just to call execution_block and loop_registry.
findings.recommendation: Split along the existing seams, moving code without changing behavior. Tool assembly, prompts, the lease keeper, settlement and dispatch each get a module with public names. Make job dispatch the only module that imports both the goal loop and the workflow runner, and have it pass its own drive function to both as the child driver, since run_goal and run_workflow drive children through _drive today; then neither imports dispatch back. Keep temporary re-exports in goal_loop.py until tests/db moves to the public names.
findings.sketch:
application/loop_tools.py     loop_registry, SummarizationOff        <- tool_catalog, workflow_runner, goal_loop
application/loop_prompts.py   SYSTEM_PROMPT, opening(goal), scope_guidance(conn, run_id, goal)
application/lease_keeper.py   keep_lease(database_url, lease, config): async context manager
application/settlement.py     finish_pass (was _finish), loop_result (was _result), run_status,
                              settle_cancellation (was _settle_children + _cancel_stray_child)
application/job_dispatch.py   process_next, drive (was _drive), execution_block
                              imports goal_loop.run_goal and workflow_runner.run_workflow and passes
                              `drive` to both as the child driver, so neither imports it back
application/goal_loop.py      LoopConfig, LoopResult, run_goal(..., drive_child), build_stage, settle_candidate
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 'small cohesive modules' and the DH-03 application/ layout. Code moves only: lease checks, fencing, receipts and transaction boundaries stay in the same functions, and the db profile proves the move.
findings.verifierNote: Line ranges, the 22 definitions and every importer confirmed. An import scan finds ten test files using goal_loop's private names, not seven. The sketch now injects the child driver, because run_goal and drive_child call _drive, and a dispatcher that both import would otherwise bring the cycle back.

findings.title: Stop codes are bare strings, and any code missing from PAUSE_FOR fails the run permanently

locations.note: PAUSE_FOR: 19 codes, 9 of them FailureClass values retyped as literals
NOT_OURS: no comment says what it means
None verifies, PAUSE_FOR suspends, everything else fails
the pass outcome as a nested string conditional
STOPPING: another code set that feeds _finish
codes built with an f-string from the counter name, so grep can't find them
credential_invalid becomes invalid_credential before PAUSE_FOR sees it
a consumer compares outcome and code with literals

findings.impact: A new or misspelled code silently becomes a terminal FAILED run, which can never resume. Knowing what any code does means reading five sets in three modules.
findings.recommendation: Add a StopCode StrEnum and an explicit disposition table that maps every code reaching _finish to its current behavior. Then derive PAUSE_FOR and NOT_OURS from the table, and type LoopResult.outcome. Add a test that every FailureClass value, AdmissionRefused code, LimitReached counter and STOPPING member has a disposition. Whether an unmapped code should suspend instead of fail is a separate decision for the owner.
findings.ruleCheck: SP-010 (terminal runs cannot resume) and DH-06 'explicit enums/unions'. Mapping each code to its current disposition first changes no behavior. StopCode is a reason code, not a second run-state enum, and stays separate from DTOs.
findings.verifierNote: Counted 19 PAUSE_FOR codes (nine are FailureClass values), five routing sets and 19 LoopStopped raises in loop_middleware.py; no test names PAUSE_FOR or NOT_OURS.

findings.title: _finish mixes the stop decision with cancellation settlement and raw job writes, and reads the status three times

locations.note: 86 lines, C901 11, no docstring, 14 callers in two modules
first status read
second read, compared with the literal 'cancelling'
job requeued with a raw UPDATE
classify_interrupted with generation + 1, to include this owner's receipts
third read, then a raw job release
CommandRefused recorded as lease_lost
outcome derived from the final code

findings.impact: Every goal and workflow pass ends here, yet its decision table can only be exercised through a disposable database. The three status reads can disagree under a concurrent pause or cancel; apply_command re-validates under locks, so the cost is muddled reporting rather than a wrong write. A refused command is reported as a lost lease, so a parent's assignment sees 'lost' for what was a state conflict.
findings.recommendation: Read status and ownership once, decide with a pure function, then run the effects. Keep the generation and status='claimed' guards on the job writes, keep classify_interrupted before FINISH_CANCEL, and keep the transition and its stop_reason in one transaction. Give a refused command its own stop code.
findings.ruleCheck: SP-010 cancellation rules and SP-012 fencing: apply_command still re-validates under row locks, job writes keep their generation predicates, and nothing reaches FINISH_CANCEL before outstanding work is classified.
findings.verifierNote: Opened every cited line; the reads at 703, 709 and 732 and the CommandRefused-to-lease_lost mapping are as stated. The impact now notes that apply_command's own checks keep the writes safe, so the gain is clarity, testability and honest reporting.

findings.title: admit_run takes 15 parameters and a binding typed Any that four different shapes satisfy

locations.note: 15 parameters, 124 lines
binding: Any decides tool grants and instructions
inherit silently replaces binding
policy is optional in the signature but required at runtime
16-column positional insert with eight conditional expressions
SimpleNamespace binding; also workflows.py:397 and improvements.py:392
binding built with type('Binding', (), {...})()
RunBinding, the typed shape, whose non-optional fields the namespaces can't meet

findings.evidence:
binding: Any = None,
    inherit: Inheritance | None = None,
    ...
    if inherit is not None:
        binding = inherit
The six callers pass a RunBinding (api/run_routes.py:264), SimpleNamespace objects (routines, workflows, improvements) whose session or Expert fields are None where RunBinding declares them non-optional, a class built with type() (browse_trial), or an Inheritance through inherit (assignments). The binding fills GoalSpec.allowed_tools and instructions (runs.py:283-284) and part of the idempotency fingerprint (runs.py:209). One function resolves a repeated goal, computes the fingerprint, checks continuation and performs six inserts.
findings.impact: Nothing checks at the type level the scope a run is admitted with, mypy strict accepts any object, and policy=None fails only at runtime. Every admission edit is high-stakes, because the receipt fingerprint must stay byte-identical for replays.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a frozen RunAdmission request, a typed RunScope with optional session and Expert fields, and an origin union, so that 'a policy unless inherited' is a type rule. Extract the fingerprint, the continuation check and the inserts. Keep request_hash's payload byte-identical, with a golden test against today's hashes, and keep run, job, first event and receipt in one transaction.

    fingerprint = admission_fingerprint(admission, goal)       # same payload as today
    async with conn.transaction():

             # _insert_goal_spec, append_event, store_receipt
findings.ruleCheck: SP-012 and SP-014: the admitted run, job, first event and receipt still commit together. Decision 0015's started_by rule is unchanged, and RunAccepted and other DTOs stay separate from the request type.

findings.title: Display redaction keeps its own three-pattern regex, weaker than the log redaction

locations.note: _SECRETS: sk-, Bearer (capitalized only) and eyJ
public_text, imported by 7 other modules, 26 calls in src
_SECRET: 11 alternatives, including tvly-, jina_, GitHub tokens and credentialed URLs
tests cover only sk-or and Bearer

findings.evidence: run_projection.py:59-61 compiles three alternatives: sk- followed by 4 or more characters, Bearer with a capital B, and eyJ tokens. The log redactor matches sk-or-, sk-, tvly-, jina_, ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_, github_pat_, bearer in any case, JWTs, credentialed database and HTTP URLs, and password or token assignments. Re-run in memory: public_text leaves tvly-, jina_, ghp_ and github_pat_ tokens, a lowercase bearer value and https://user:pass@host intact, while logs.redact masks every one. public_text sanitizes plans, summaries, evidence, goal labels and run-list text written by the model, for display in the UI. Its importers are four api route modules, memory.py, workflows.py and operations/route_qualification.py.
findings.impact: A Tavily, Jina or GitHub token that a model echoes into a plan or summary is redacted in the logs but shown to workspace members, although the projection's own comment (run_projection.py:58) says a key the model was shown must not be displayed. Each new tool key widens the gap, because nothing ties the two lists together.
findings.recommendation: Keep the token shapes in one pure module that both logs.redact and public_text use. Display keeps its 500-character cut and can skip the key=value heuristic. Share one fixture list of token shapes across both modules' tests.
findings.sketch:
# autobots/domain/secrets.py: pure, no I/O
TOKEN_SHAPES: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (SK_OR, SK, TAVILY, JINA, GITHUB_CLASSIC, GITHUB_PAT,
                                        BEARER_ANY_CASE, JWT, CREDENTIALED_URL)   # one list, one owner
_TOKENS = re.compile('|'.join(TOKEN_SHAPES))
def mask_tokens(text: str) -> str: return _TOKENS.sub('[redacted]', text)

# operations/logs.py  redact(text)      = mask identifiers and key=value pairs, then mask_tokens(text)
# run views           public_text(text) = mask_tokens(text)[:limit]
# tests               one TOKEN_FIXTURES list asserted against both redact and public_text
findings.ruleCheck: SP-011 (the public projection never exposes secrets) and python-worker.md 'sanitized public projections'; Decision 0025 V2 states the same principle for stored keys. The change only widens display redaction and keeps log redaction's coverage, so no guardrail is loosened.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced the gap in memory for every token shape listed. The rule check now cites SP-011 ('never exposes secrets') as the governing rule, and the change risk is medium rather than low because the shared module also feeds log redaction.

findings.title: apply_command packs replay, ownership, guard, cancel cascade and job rules into one 97-line transaction

locations.note: 11 parameters, C901 13
a receipt applies only when both actor_id and idempotency_key are given
live-claim test, first copy
cancel side effects inline, recursing into apply_command for children
second copy, overriding _job_status
third copy

_job_status, the pure part of the rule

findings.impact: After each transition, a rule decides whether a worker or nobody owns the run. It is split across _job_status and two inline overrides on a tuple, and can only be tested against a database.
findings.recommendation: Name the locked job row and make the post-transition job status one pure, unit-tested function. Move the cancel side effects into a helper. Make the receipt an optional parameter object, so the actor and key are passed together or not at all. Keep the lock order (job row, then run row), the version check and the receipt in the one transaction.
findings.ruleCheck: SP-010 'atomic domain update/outbox event' and SP-012 ownership checked in the writing transaction: everything stays inside the same transaction and lock order; only code moves.
findings.verifierNote: Opened apply_command and its helpers; the three positional live-claim tests and the paired receipt condition are as stated.

findings.title: Run and job state are written from four modules, beside the command table rather than through it

locations.note: the claim writes queued to running with record_transition and never consults next_status
RunCommand.CLAIM is never issued, and neither is REPAIR (line 90)
job requeued with a literal status
job released with a literal status
read the version, then apply: one of 7 copies
another copy
cascade cancel issued as Actor.USER
approval expiry, run by the worker, pauses the run as Actor.USER

findings.evidence: The domain table (domain/runs.py:24-125) is the guard, and apply_command enforces it under locks. Around it, run or job rows are written directly in four modules: the claim transition in worker_leases.py bypasses next_status; job rows get literal statuses in runs.py:477, worker_leases.py:90 and goal_loop.py:714 and 735; and operations/browse_trial.py:213 sets status='running' itself after its claim. Seven call sites (goal_loop.py:457, 564, 624 and 748, workflow_runner.py:346, approvals.py:66, assignments.py:279) read the run's version and pass it straight back. Four system actions (runs.py:355, goal_loop.py:634, approvals.py:227, assignments.py:292) are issued as Actor.USER because the table has only USER and WORKER, and the status event (runs.py:96-97) records no actor. Total: 4 job writers + 7 version-read copies + 4 system commands issued as USER.
findings.impact: To answer 'what can move this run or its job', an engineer has to read several modules. A guard added to the CLAIM entry would not apply to claims, and guards and events can't tell a cascaded or expiry-driven command from a person's.
findings.recommendation: Give the application one transitions surface. It should offer apply_command for people, and apply_worker_command(lease, ...), which reads the version and writes stop_reason in the same transaction. Add cascade_command with an explicit system actor, a claim that calls next_status(CLAIM), and named job helpers with a JobStatus enum. Keep every generation and status='claimed' predicate as it is.

findings.title: The invocation ledger's states, failure classes and spend formula are restated as literals in five modules

locations.note: ACTIVE and OUTSTANDING, the only named sets
admission's spend formula, again at 308-310
status guard as a SQL literal, SET clause built with an f-string
a second writer of reserved-to-cancelled and dispatched-to-uncertain
'charge_not_reported', a failure class outside FailureClass
'reserved' and 'dispatched' restated
comment: the public figures can't drift from what admission counted
the projection's own spend formula, copied at 446-450

findings.evidence: The six invocation states (reserved, dispatched, succeeded, failed_before_acceptance, uncertain, cancelled) have no enum, and both ModelAdmission and recovery.classify_interrupted change them. Four failure classes live outside FailureClass: charge_not_reported, worker_lost, cancelled_after_dispatch and cancelled. Admission counts spend as the reservation while an attempt is outstanding and the charge otherwise. The projection computes two separate sums with an extra reconciled_at filter, and workflow_overview.py:24 holds a third copy. About 14 literal sites, counted by reading the 13 files plus grep for reconciled_at and the status lists.
findings.impact: SP-008 requires shared root and workspace accounting, and SP-010 asks for documented state machines kept separate from run status, which the model-call ledger lacks. Today a new status or failure class has to be found in five files, and nothing enforces the comment that promises the public figures match admission.
findings.recommendation: Add InvocationStatus and settlement-reason enums beside FailureClass, and make ModelAdmission the only writer (recovery calls a method on it). Define spend once, either as a SQL view or function in a forward migration or as one shared SQL fragment. Add a test that admission and projection agree on a seeded ledger.
findings.ruleCheck: SP-008 (reserve before dispatch, shared accounting) and SP-010's separately documented state machines. Migrations only move forward, and the reservation and settlement rules are unchanged.
findings.verifierNote: Opened every cited writer and formula. SP-010 names steps, tool attempts, approvals and credentials for documented state machines, so the model-call ledger is covered by extension; the impact and rule check now say so instead of quoting a rule SP-010 doesn't state.

findings.title: Run views read one run with 7 to 19 statements and no common snapshot

@asynccontextmanager
async def snapshot_read(conn) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    async with conn.transaction():           # opened before any other statement on this connection

        yield

findings.title: The lease keeper is started and stopped by hand in three places, and its cancelled task is never awaited

locations.note: create_task in run_goal
cancel without await
the same pair in _settle_candidate

findings.evidence:
beating = asyncio.create_task(_keep_lease(database_url, lease, config))
    ...
    finally:
        beating.cancel()
        await end_segment(connection, lease.run_id)
findings.impact: Each new kind of pass has to copy the pattern. A cancelled task that nobody awaits closes its connection at some later point. A programming error in discount_sleep becomes a quiet reconnect loop while the lease keeps being extended, because the beat runs before the discount.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the keeper in an async context manager that cancels and then awaits the task, as operations/worker.py does for its heartbeat. Split one look into a method that unit tests can drive with the injected WakeClock.
findings.sketch:
@asynccontextmanager
async def keep_lease(database_url, lease, config, clock=None) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    task = asyncio.create_task(_LeaseKeeper(database_url, lease, config, clock).run())
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        task.cancel()
        await asyncio.wait({task})     # cleanup finished; the caller's own cancellation still propagates

class _LeaseKeeper:
    async def run(self) -> None: ...             # reconnect loop
    async def _look(self, conn) -> bool: ...     # one tick: wake check, beat or revive, discount
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 'propagate cancellation after cleanup' and SP-012 heartbeats by database time. The heartbeat, revive and discount SQL and their order (beat before discount) are unchanged.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed the three create_task and cancel pairs, the unawaited cancels, the broad retry loop, and that operations/worker.py:158-160 awaits its heartbeat task after cancelling it.
